info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Generated from the live router — every operation below is a route the unified cloud binary actually serves. Tagged by product: the first path segment after /v1/.

get.summary: listSyncs returns every sync link in the caller's org, with each link's last
get.description:
listSyncs returns every sync link in the caller's org, with each link's last
reconcile time.

post.summary: createSync links a source repository to a target and stores the sync policy.
post.description:
createSync links a source repository to a target and stores the sync policy. It
is an UPSERT — re-stating the same source→target pair updates that link rather
than making a second one — and with run set it reconciles once immediately in the
background. The org comes from the validated principal, never the body, so a link
can only bind endpoints within the caller's own org.

delete.summary:
deleteSync removes a sync link and tears down its derived outbound mirror, so an
unsynced repository can never keep pushing to the upstream.
delete.description:
deleteSync removes a sync link and tears down its derived outbound mirror, so an
unsynced repository can never keep pushing to the upstream. Answers 204.

get.description: getSync returns one sync link. A link in another org reads as not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sync id, as returned by create.

patch.summary:
patchSync updates a link's mutable policy — direction, trigger, actor — in place;
an omitted field is left alone.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sync id from the path.

post.summary:
runSync reconciles one link now — the manual re-sync, and the initial import for a
source that cannot webhook.
post.description:
runSync reconciles one link now — the manual re-sync, and the initial import for a
source that cannot webhook. It answers 202 immediately and the reconcile runs in a
bounded background worker, so a large mirror-in never blocks the request.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sync id, as returned by create.

connector.description: Connector optionally names the stored credential to authenticate with.

locator.description: Locator addresses the resource — an https clone URL for git, a repo name natively.

provider.description: Provider is the platform: github or gitlab for a source, native for a target.

id.description: ID echoes the sync being reconciled.

queued.description: Queued is always true — the reconcile runs in a bounded background worker.

data.description: Data is the org's links; an empty array when nothing is synced.

actor.description: Actor is the loop-guard identity whose own writes are ignored.

direction.description: Direction is both, pull, push or off.

id.description: ID is the sync id from the path.

trigger.description: Trigger is webhook, poll or manual.

id.description: ID is the sync id, as returned by create.

actor.description:
Actor is the loop-guard identity whose own writes are ignored; empty takes
GIT_SYNC_ACTOR.

direction.description: Direction is both, pull, push or off; empty means both.

kind.description: Kind is the sync family; empty means git, the only kind today.

run.description: Run reconciles once in the background as soon as the link is stored.

source.description:
Source is the upstream side: provider github or gitlab, an https clone URL on
that provider's own host, no userinfo. Required.

target.description:
Target is the downstream side; omit it for git and it derives a native Hanzo
Git repo named after the source.

trigger.description: Trigger is webhook, poll or manual; empty means webhook.

updatedAt.description: bumped on every reconcile — the last-synced time
